# Neko Health (Stockholm / London / NYC — full-body scan clinics)

URL: https://www.nekohealth.com/us/en

## Type system
- Display: `Orleans, "Orleans Fallback", Georgia, serif` — H1 at 100px/400,
  H2 at 68px/400. A proper serif carries every headline, which is unusual
  for a body-scanning/AI-health-tech brand; it reads more editorial/quiet
  than clinical.
- Body: `"IBM Plex Sans", "IBM Plex Sans Fallback", system-ui, sans-serif`
  at 16px/400 — a technical/mono-adjacent grotesk pairs the serif headline
  with an engineering-flavoured body face, hinting at the hardware behind
  the brand without shouting it.
- No mono typeface visible on the homepage.

## Color system (converted from oklch via canvas sampling)
- bg: white `#FFFFFF`.
- surface/secondary bg: pale sky blue `#DEF2F7`, used for large full-bleed
  section backgrounds (the "Opening in NYC" globe section).
- accent: soft yellow `#FFF597`, used as a large closing-CTA section
  background — the one warm, high-contrast note against an otherwise cool
  palette.
- text/dark: navy-black `#01202C` and charcoal `#262C2E`; secondary text
  `#496970` (a muted teal-grey).
- neutral surfaces: `#E7EDEE`, `#F1F4F4`.

## Layout & grid
- Full-bleed cookie-consent-adjacent hero photo (rear view of a woman
  getting scanned) with serif headline overlaid directly on the image.
- Below the hero, sections alternate white and pale-blue backgrounds in
  large, single-column blocks — a soft, low-contrast rhythm rather than a
  dense grid.
- A small light-blue globe/map illustration marks the "Opening in NYC"
  location-expansion section — an unusually playful, low-fidelity graphic
  for a health-tech brand.

## Sections (order observed)
1. Full-bleed hero photo + serif headline ("The future of preventive
   health") + waitlist CTA
2. "Introducing the Neko Health Scan" — pale blue section, short copy,
   "Learn more" pill button
3. "Opening in NYC on Sep 24, 2026" — globe illustration, waitlist CTA
4. "Cutting-edge technology meets first-class care" — white card on pale
   blue background
5. Testimonial quotes (two-column, understated)
6. "Why people choose Neko" — three short value props
7. "Questions. Answered." — accordion FAQ
8. Press logos (GQ, NYT, The Guardian, Wallpaper)
9. Yellow closing CTA band ("A completely new healthcare experience")
10. Dark footer

## Components/signature
- Serif display type on a health-tech scanning company — the single most
  distinctive move in the set; it borrows luxury-editorial type cues
  instead of the SaaS-grotesk default.
- The pale-blue-to-yellow palette shift at the very end of the page acts as
  a visual "wake up" cue right before the final CTA.

## Motion/interactions
- Understated; no visible dashboard, chart, or biomarker table on the
  homepage — the "Health Scan" product page (linked, not shown here) is
  presumably where numeric detail lives. The marketing homepage stays
  almost entirely qualitative.

## Biomarker/trust presentation
- No scores or charts on the homepage. Trust is carried by press logos
  (GQ, NYT, Guardian, Wallpaper), a testimonial pull-quote, and repeated
  claims of "beautifully designed, incredibly data-driven" — the brand
  asserts scientific rigor in prose rather than visualizing it up front.

## What works
- Demonstrates that a hardware-heavy, data-driven scanning company can
  still choose a serif-led, editorial-calm identity instead of a
  dashboard-first one — makes the brand feel considered and premium rather
  than "gadget."
- The restrained two-tone palette (pale blue + one yellow CTA band) avoids
  the generic medical blue-on-white look by using an unusually soft, almost
  pastel blue rather than a saturated clinical blue.

## Avoid
- Very light body-text contrast (`#496970` on pale backgrounds) needs
  checking at small sizes — the calm palette can tip into low-legibility
  if pushed further.
- Homepage withholds almost all quantitative/biomarker content — fine for
  brand marketing, but don't copy this pattern if the product's actual
  differentiator is data density.

## How to apply
- Pair a quiet serif display with a technical/engineering-flavoured
  grotesk body face to signal "considered hardware, not generic startup."
- Use a single pastel hue (not saturated clinical blue) as the dominant
  secondary background, and reserve one warm accent (yellow, coral) purely
  for the final conversion moment.
